newsitem.title: RWANDA: Eastern Zaire rebels advance on Shaba, U.N. source.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Zaire rebels advance on Shaba, U.N. source.

text.p: Eastern Zaire rebels are advancing towards mineral-producing Shaba province and have seized the town of Lulimba despite a government counter-offensive, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.
"We have received information the rebels have taken the town of Lulimba southwest of Fizi," said the official, who declined to be identified, in the Rwandan capital of Kigali.
"They are heading southwest right the other side of Fizi."
Lulimba town is 60 km (38 miles) southwest of Fizi and only some 30 km (19 miles) north of the border of Shaba province.
Zaire said earlier on Wednesday thousands of Ugandan troops had invaded its territory including one group heading for Shaba but Uganda immediately dismissed the accusation as laughable.

A military high command statement said about 2,000 Ugandan troops had left Fizi -- about 350 km (about 200 miles) southwest of the border with Uganda -- and were heading in the direction of Kalemie in Shaba.

"It is absolute falsehood. It is in fact laughable that we would be so stupid as to openly send troops into Zaire. Even the geographical locations mentioned do not make sense," Hope Kivengere, spokeswoman for President Yoweri Museveni, told Reuters by telephone from Kampala.
"The Zairean statement lacks credibility. We have not sent any troops at all to Zaire," Kivengere added.
In Brussels, the Belgian Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday it was concerned about reports on the presence of foreign troops in Zaire which, if confirmed, would be totally unacceptable.

"We are receiving more and more reports about the presence of regular Rwandan troops in eastern Zaire. If these can be confirmed, this would be an unacceptable violation of the territorial integrity of Zaire," spokesman Andre Querton said.
He said the reports spoke of a "meaningful number" of Rwandan units in the Kivu area, who had moved into the region after the seizure of eastern Zaire by Zairean rebels.
Rwanda has denied it sent its troops to fight alongside the Rwandan-backed rebels who launched their revolt in October.

In the most comprehensive charge against the Kampala government, Zaire also said a brigade of Ugandan troops equipped with Russian-made anti-aircraft missiles had taken position at Beni about 50 km (35 miles) from the Ugandan border south of the mining town Bunia.
It said 200 mercenaries from Eritrea, Ethiopia and Somalia landed in the last few days in Goma, the biggest Zairean town seized by rebels who started fighting the army last October.
Rebel leaders say their objective is to overthrow the central governemt in Kinshasa. The government has launched a counter-offensive backed by hundreds of European mercenaries.
